record: Spread 23-11 · ML 27-7 · POTD L
summary: None of the 11 spread losses were bad beats - 2 were close losses (CLE, MEM in OT) and the other 9 were real misses.

record: Spread 2-3 · ML 5-0 · POTD W
summary: Light five-game CBB night: every favorite won (ML 5-0) but sides went 2-3, and both spread wins were backdoor covers. No bad beats - UK was a garbage-time close loss and the other two misses were real.
went_well: Not much to credit on the sides: Drexel +31.5 and Sam Houston +26.5 only got there with late garbage-time runs after trailing by 36 and 32, so those were lucky wins, not proof. The ML read was right across the board, and the Sam Houston pick did correctly bake in Alabama playing without Holloway.
went_wrong: Wofford +26.5 leaned on Tennessee's ugly exhibitions, but the Vols ran away with a 36-10 burst after half - a bad read on early-season noise. UAPB +38.5 counted on Calipari resting starters, and Arkansas won by 45 anyway; the market (and Kalshi at -40.5) had the better number. UK -32.5 was a tiny 1.5-pt edge on a huge number and the bench gave it back late.
improve: New L004: in CBB games with a 25+ point spread, only take the underdog when the model's edge is 5+ points - big dogs are 4-4 over two days with both of today's wins being backdoors, while laying 23.5+ is 7-3.

record: Spread 9-5 · ML 9-5 · POTD L

The road-dominance read on POR -3.5 (won by 13) and fading tired Toronto with DEN -4.5 (won by 19) were right too; NOP -5.5 only got there in OT, so don't count that one.

improve: New L005: when an NBA favorite of -5+ is priced up mostly because the other team is banged up, only lay it with a 2+ pt model edge - MEM -6.5 on a 1.5-pt edge lost outright to depleted Indiana. Also treat a line move against the public as a tiebreaker, not a reason on its own: DET -2.5 leaned on that and lost by 6.

record: Spread 6-5 · ML 10-1 · POTD W

went_wrong: Both small-edge plays on short-handed teams were bad reads: Ravens +10.5 with a rookie QB lost by 23 after three turnovers, and Orlando without Banchero and Suggs coughed it up 25 times and lost by 13 to a Suns team on a back-to-back. improve: New L006: when backing a team missing its starting QB or two-plus starters, require a 2+ point edge or side with the healthy team - it's the mirror of L005, which keeps us from overrating those injuries the other way. Keep using L004 on 25+ CBB spreads (3-0 so far), but don't change how we handle laying big CBB numbers off one 4-3 night - TTU and ARIZ were the market being right, not a pattern yet.

season:
- 306 games graded since Nov 2.
- Against the spread, all games: 153-152-1 (50.2%, 95% range 45-56%). That's basically a coin flip and still under the 52.4% break-even, which is normal for the data-collection phase.
- Official plays (started Nov 13): 6-3 (67%). Way too few to mean anything yet.
- Closing line value: 36 picks beat the closing number and 12 got a worse one (average +0.14 points). That's the most encouraging sign so far, but part of it comes from taking the better number between DraftKings and FanDuel.
- Favorites 118-104 (53%), underdogs 35-48-1 (42%). Taking points with underdogs has hurt; L011 is testing that.
- By edge size: under 1 pt 53-58 (48%), 1-2 pts 59-55-1 (52%), 2-3 pts 28-23 (55%), 3+ pts 13-16 (45%). The 3+ point edges doing worst fits the "big edges are a warning" rule.
- By league: NFL 18-11 (62%), NBA 53-52 (50%), CFB 33-33 (50%), CBB 49-56-1 (47%). NFL looks best but it's a small sample.
- By week: week of Nov 2 86-65 (57%), week of Nov 9 67-87-1 (44%). That swing is mostly normal noise, a good reminder that hot and cold stretches don't last.
- The moneyline record of 237-68-1 (78%) looks great but is misleading: it's high mostly because the model usually picks the favorite.

summary: The one official play, Seton Hall +4.5 (also the POTD), won outright over Wisconsin, and the full board went 7-6 ATS and 9-4 straight up with CLV slightly negative (-0.2). No bad beats: of the 6 losses, the Knicks-Wolves game was a normal close loss and the other 5 were real misses.
went_well: Seton Hall +4.5 and Notre Dame +3.5 were good dog reads that won outright, and Memphis -7.5 against a Warriors team missing Curry and Green won by 28. The big CBB dogs Stetson +35.5 and Southern Utah +38.5 covered easily, and Milwaukee +10.5 got there by the hook, which is closer to luck than proof.
went_wrong: Kansas +2.5, West Virginia +9.5 and Spurs -15.5 were 'line was right' losses where the market's number held up, and Indy +12.5 (an L018 play) and Tarleton +26.5 (an L017 dog) were bad reads that lost by 23 and 45.
improve: Nothing new to add: the misses fit lessons already being tested (L016 now 4-4-1, L017 5-7, L018 4-3), so keep collecting rather than react to one day. The morning run should tag L002 when it caps a neutral-site major-conference CBB edge; three of those games ran Nov 19 and L002 still has zero tagged picks.

record: Official 1-2 · Spread 8-15 · ML 17-6 · POTD W · CLV +0.2
summary: Rough night: the official plays went 1-2 (Indiana -2.5 won, Oklahoma State +1.5 and Xavier -2.5 lost), and the full board went 8-15 ATS but 17-6 straight up with a small positive CLV (+0.2). Of the 15 ATS losses, one was a bad beat (Utah +4.5), three were close ones (Detroit, Chicago, Orlando) and the rest were real misses.
went_well: Indiana over Kentucky was the right read on the better team and won by 14, and Atlanta -6.5 beat the closing number by a point and covered by 7.5. Sacramento +14.5, UCF +18.5 and Georgia Tech +8.5 were dogs that were never in real danger; Loyola +42.5 cashing by the hook was luck, not proof.
went_wrong: Xavier -2.5 and Oklahoma State +1.5 (both official) were bad reads that lost by 18 and 15, and Duke -13.5 lost outright to Clemson. The huge CBB dogs Manhattan, Mississippi Valley State and Eastern Illinois all got buried, and OKC -10.5 and Houston +1.5 were spots where the market's number held up.
improve: Nothing new to add from one night: the big-dog misses are what L017 (now 7-10) and L004 are already testing, Orlando was another L011 loss (13-19) and Indiana +6.5 another L012 loss (2-7), so keep collecting. The morning run should still tag L002 on neutral-site major-conference CBB games; Oklahoma State-Minnesota and Kentucky-Indiana were candidates and went untagged.

record: Official 1-5 · Spread 20-24 · ML 32-12 · POTD W · CLV +0.3
summary: Tough Saturday for the official plays at 1-5: only Tennessee +1.5 won, while Memphis +6.5, Ohio State -3.5, UNC +1.5, Baylor +5.5 and Arizona -7.5 lost. The full board went 20-24 ATS (NBA 5-1, CBB 3-1, CFB 12-22) and 32-12 straight up with a small positive CLV. Of the 24 ATS losses, one was a real bad beat (Memphis at Navy), three were close or OT ones (Arizona by the hook in OT, Northwestern on a last-second FG, BYU in 3OT), and the rest were real misses.
went_well: Tennessee +1.5 was the right read on a home team the ratings called a pick'em and won by 14. The NBA side was sharp: San Antonio -16.5 and Portland +5.5 both beat the close by 2 points, Dallas -5.5 covered, and Villanova +4.5 won outright. Wake-GT +21.5, Notre Dame -20.5 and Oklahoma State -2.5 all cashed by a half point, so those don't prove much.
went_wrong: Ohio State -3.5 and UNC +1.5 (both official) were bad reads: Nebraska led most of the game, and UNC was down to a freshman QB who threw two picks. NC State over FSU, Wisconsin over Purdue and San Diego State over Boise were big misses, and Texas Tech, Miami and LSU-Queens were spots where the market's number held up.
improve: No new lesson from one rough Saturday. CFB is 46-57 ATS on the season (45%), which is still close to normal noise for 103 games. The picks flipped onto the ratings side by L018 went 2-5 (now 6-10), and L011 went 2-0 (now 15-19), so keep collecting on both. Before locking an official CFB play, the pregame check should confirm the starting QB for both teams (UNC's starter was out). If that keeps costing us, it could become a CFB version of L006.
